title: The constant of integration and initial conditions
keyIdea: + C means a whole family of curves; one known point picks out the curve you want.

kid: When you integrate, you get a family of curves. They all have the same shape, just moved up or down. That is the + C.
If you know one point on the curve, put its x and y into your answer. Then you can work out C and pick the right curve.
adult: Given dy/dx = f(x) and a point (x₀, y₀), integrate to get y = F(x) + C, then substitute: C = y₀ − F(x₀).
In science this point is often an initial condition, such as a starting position at t = 0. With t = 0 many terms vanish, so C is simply the starting value.

familyTip: Trace one curve, then slide the tracing paper straight up. Every copy has the same slopes. Which copy goes through a dot you drew?

practice.prompt: dy/dx = 2x, and the curve passes through (0, {c}). Find C in y = x² + C.
practice.hint: Put x = 0 and y = {c} into y = x² + C.

practice.prompt: y = x² + C passes through (2, {y}). Find C.
How are the curves y = x² + 1 and y = x² + 5 related?
choices: Same shape; one is 4 units higher
practice.hint: Compare them at the same x.
practice.explain: At every x, the second is 4 more: the same curve moved up 4.

practice.prompt: dy/dx = 3x², and y = {c} when x = 1. Find C in y = x³ + C.

pool.prompt: y = x² + C passes through (3, {y}). Find C.
dy/dx = 4x³, and y = {y} when x = 1. Find y when x = 2.
pool.hint: Integrate to y = x⁴ + C, find C, then put x = 2.

pool.prompt: Why can't you find C from dy/dx alone?
choices: Every vertical shift has the same gradient
pool.hint: Do the shifted curves have different slopes?
pool.explain: Moving a curve up or down doesn't change its gradient, so dy/dx can't tell them apart.

pool.prompt: A position is s = 5t² + C metres, and s = {h} when t = 0. Find C.
y = 2x + C passes through (1, 5). What is C?
y = x³ + C passes through (2, {y}). Find C.
What is enough to fix C?
choices: Any one point on the curve
pool.explain: One known point gives one equation, which is enough to find C.

visual.caption: Slide C until the curve y = x² + C passes through the red point (1, 4).
